summary: Planned office building on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (office, laboratory and life science uses are permitted there), paired with Block 12 (the project's engineer describes the two together as about 430,000 sq ft of office, while the Planning Department's October 2020 Phase 1 approval lists about 219,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 11 and 177,000 for Block 12); design was under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report. In a request reported July 29, 2026, the developer asked to raise Block 11's height by 15 feet; the Planning Commission approved the amendment unanimously (reported Aug 3, 2026) and the Board of Supervisors passed the amended development agreement on first reading on Sept 29, 2026, and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Mayor 'APPROVED'). No construction start found.

milestones.text: Blocks 11, 12 and 15 covered together at a community pre-application meeting for design review

'Blocks 11 and 12 Design Review Application' dated February 2021 (the 2024 annual compliance report gives both February 24, 2021 and February 4, 2021 for it); the report cites it for the Block 11 childcare space ('Included in designs of B11ground floor') and for La Cocina PDR space 'designed into Blocks 11 + 12', exact space to be determined (the report does not place La Cocina in Block 11 specifically)
2024 annual compliance report states designs for Blocks 11 and 12 'are under review' (i.e., not yet approved) as of report submission

Developer requests a Development Agreement amendment increasing Block 11's permitted height by 15 feet, to make its 'smaller floorplate' more attractive to commercial tenants; the Chronicle's July 29, 2026 article says the Planning Commission considered the request 'On Thursday' (the hearing date is not stated there) and that the Planning Department had recommended approval; the SF Standard reported on August 3, 2026 that 'The commissioners approved unanimously, sending the decision to the Board of Supervisors'; the Board of Supervisors then passed the amendment package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (next entry)

Board of Supervisors passes the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770) on first reading; Legistar's history lists '9/29/2026 ... Board of Supervisors ... PASSED, ON FIRST READING ... Pass' for both. The Mayor's approval and enactment on October 13, 2026 are the next milestone. All dates here are legislative event dates as listed by the Clerk of the Board (first-reading row read October 12 and again October 14, 2026)

Mayor approves the Amended and Restated Development Agreement (BOS File 260724) and the Planning Code and Zoning Map ordinance for the Potrero Power Station Special Use District (BOS File 260770): Legistar lists both as 'Status: Passed' with 'Final action: 10/13/2026', 'Enactment date: 10/13/2026' and enactment numbers 208-26 (File 260724) and 209-26 (File 260770), and a history row '10/13/2026 ... Mayor ... APPROVED' for each. The Board of Supervisors' own 10/6/2026 history row still shows no action or result ('Not available'), so no Board vote on that date is shown. The date is the enactment date, from the Clerk of the Board's listing (page read October 14, 2026); it is an event date, not a Board vote result.

Completion expected: Block 11 is part of Phase 1 (per the 2024 annual compliance report's Phase 1 list, Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, 15); SocketSite's October 2020 'Re-Phase Program, Detailed Construction Schedule' table gives Block 11 vertical development 2025 to 2027 (the same article's text says the first phase would be completed in 2028, and its table runs Block 12 to 2029 and Phase 1 open space to 2029); a 2020 forecast, not a current Block 11 date
milestones.basis_note: Phase 1 in the October 2020 Phase 1 and Phasing Plan Amendment ('Phase 1 Development Schedule: Years 2020 - 2029'); SocketSite (Oct 9, 2020): its text says 'the first phase of development would be completed in 2028' and its schedule table lists Block 11 vertical development 2025 to 2027 (Block 12 2027 to 2029, Phase 1 open space 2025 to 2029, Block 15 2023 to 2026), so the article is not consistent with itself; this milestone uses Block 11's own table row. Soft: a 2020 forecast -- design for Blocks 11/12 was still 'under review' (not approved) as of the March 2025 compliance report, and in July 2026 the developer asked to raise Block 11's height; the Board passed an amended Phasing Plan package on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 (BOS File 260724) whose Block 11 timing has not been read here.

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 11 as a development block; the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. (Block 11 was later named one of Phase 1's six blocks by the October 2020 Phase 1 Development Phase Application -- a construction-phase assignment, not when it first entered the plan.)

details.text: 2026 height amendment for Block 11: the Sept 28, 2026 draft Design for Development attached to the Amended and Restated Development Agreement labels Block 11 '145' Maximum' in its Block 11 controls (Appendix A.10), where the adopted D4D's Appendix A.10 labels it '130' Maximum'; the amendment package was enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar), but the final text and the date it takes effect were not read, so the 130 ft adopted limit is the one this record still shows.

Floor area of Block 11, further detail: Meyers+ describes the Blocks 11 and 12 office space as having below-grade parking, and the October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists Block 11 with 5,000 sq ft retail, 6,000 PDR, 6,000 childcare and about 48,500 accessory parking besides its commercial space.

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 11; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer (Meyers+). The Planning Department's October 7, 2020 Phase 1 approval lists approximately 219,000 sq ft of commercial space for Block 11 and 177,000 for Block 12 (about 396,000 together, plus retail, PDR, childcare and other uses); no source reconciles the two figures.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +15 ft height increase is tied to the Development Agreement and Planning Code amendment package (BOS Files 260724 and 260770), which passed the Board of Supervisors on first reading on Sept 29, 2026 and Legistar lists it enacted on Oct 13, 2026 (Legistar: Mayor 'APPROVED'; enactment numbers 208-26 and 209-26; page read Oct 14, 2026). The final text and the date it takes effect were not read, so this record's height fact still shows the adopted limit.

This record's map outline is DataSF Assessor lot 4232021 (active, unaddressed, recorded 2022-08-30), chosen because 77% of our earlier trace of the D4D figure lies inside it; that this lot is Block 11's own parcel is an inference from location, shape and size, and no document read names the lot.
